fences.title: Bunny is the healthy-path portrait accelerator
fences.decision: Healthy browser tabs load content-addressed portrait bytes directly from Bunny; one failed real-image probe selects the canonical first-party fallback for that tab.
fences.reason: Direct Bunny delivery avoids charging every healthy portrait read to the Cloudflare Worker budget. A resolver failure on one network is the reason the fallback exists, not evidence that Bunny should be disabled globally.
fences.change_control: Retiring or replacing Bunny requires an explicit architecture migration that updates this registry, the delivery runbook, source policy, production and staging configuration, behavioral tests, and deploy guard in one reviewed change.

fences.title: Gene discovery is eligibility-gated and range-stable
fences.decision: Complete canonical profiles are indexable through one published-catalog predicate, while aliases redirect, incomplete profiles remain noindex, unknown symbols return 404, and the crawlable archive uses frozen self-locating prefix ranges rather than numeric pages. Homepage discovery reuses the existing non-visual description instead of adding visible archive controls; accessibility skip links are clipped until focused. Decorative printed selector alternatives are CSS-rendered ink rather than peer DOM facts, while their noninteractive fields name the resolved molecular value and mapped character result. Model-training crawlers are blocked before Worker execution while AI search and user-directed retrieval agents remain allowed.
fences.reason: Agents need explicit card mappings and a link path they can choose from a known symbol, but that crawler frontier must not become perfunctory chrome that breaks the human card-gallery immersion or let model-training crawlers exhaust the shared Worker allowance. Frozen ranges provide the path without guessing, the shared eligibility gate prevents arbitrary application shells or incomplete cards from becoming an unbounded search corpus, and purpose-specific crawler policy preserves AI search without paying for training ingestion.
fences.change_control: Gene response headers, HTML metadata, homepage discovery placement, archive membership, sitemap membership, llms.txt, renderer semantics, crawler WAF policy, robots.txt, deploy reconciliation, tests, instructions, and runbook must change atomically. Range boundaries may change only through an explicit biological-inventory migration; routine catalog publications must never rebalance them. Do not add the archive to the immersive Archive/Clans switcher, expose feed skip links at rest, represent decorative selector ink as interactive controls or peer facts, or replace the purpose-specific crawler split with a blanket AI-bot block.

fences.title: Queue wakeups follow durable due times
fences.decision: Cloudflare Queue messages wake durable ledger work only when it is runnable; unfinished future work is delayed until the earliest next_attempt_at and is never polled by immediate replacement messages.
fences.reason: A single future retry otherwise creates an ack/read/delete/send feedback loop that consumes the daily Queue allowance without doing work. Short polling caps also spend retry attempts and can dead-letter a message before its durable backoff expires.
fences.change_control: Queue topology, durable status accounting, retry delays, consumer configuration, behavioral tests, instructions, and the runbook must change atomically. Any replacement must prove a bounded number of billable operations while no work is due.

fences.title: The primary Iconoplasm D1 is bounded operational state
fences.decision: The primary D1 stays below an 80% target of its 500,000,000-byte per-database wall by storing immutable profile prose once and moving publish events older than 30 days to a separately bound cold audit D1 after row-level verification.
fences.reason: Duplicated manifestation prose and an unbounded 297,818-row publish ledger filled the database and stopped all writes. The old dashboard compared the database to the unrelated 5 GB account allowance, so it reported roughly 10% usage at the per-database hard limit.
fences.change_control: Large payload placement, read-model columns, append-only ledgers, retention, archive bindings, capacity thresholds, observability, migrations, tests, instructions, runbook, and deploy enforcement must change atomically. Cold history may be removed from the hot database only after verified archival.

fences.title: Discord fulfillment is one bounded receipt per request batch and gene
fences.decision: A Free Queue action persists one batch identity; Discord delivery waits for the complete batch-and-gene group, sends one message with at most ten full-resolution preview images, and links the authoritative gene gallery for the complete result set.
fences.reason: Individual outbox rows otherwise turn ten requested candidates into ten interruptions. Completion-time or cron-window grouping is not safe because it can merge independent actions or fragment one slow action. Discord cannot carry one hundred useful image attachments in one message, and the Worker must keep memory and subrequests bounded.
fences.change_control: Request creation, batch identity and size columns, delivery-pending trigger snapshots, group completeness, attachment and memory ceilings, nonce idempotency, reconciliation, behavioral tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. Never replace the durable batch boundary with timing or row adjacency.

fences.title: Iconoplasm is static-first with one dynamic Worker invocation
fences.decision: The Iconoplasm custom hostname is owned directly by the existing stateful Worker, where matching build artifacts are served by Workers Static Assets before Worker execution and dynamic misses enter that Worker exactly once.
fences.reason: On the Free plan, the former wildcard public proxy charged one public and one internal invocation for every request, including more than one hundred static dependencies on a normal page. Asset-first delivery removes static traffic from the Worker quota and direct dynamic routing removes the redundant proxy invocation without changing vote authority or adding a state holder.
fences.change_control: Route ownership, static bundle construction and limits, security headers, rate-limit ownership, stateful bindings, deployment order, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. A replacement must be selected from current production evidence and prove equal or lower Worker use while preserving complete gene first paint and strongly ordered votes; this fence is not authority by tradition.

fences.title: Anonymous startup and extension hover use the published read plane
fences.decision: Anonymous homepage startup avoids auth, settings, inventory, and admin probes; authenticated startup is gated by a non-authoritative session-presence hint. Signed-out dossier visits persist across the full 19,023-gene browser-local shelf; an authenticated page session merges at most 200 pending symbols and retains the remainder for later sessions. Extension pages receive a separately versioned scanner artifact capped at 3 MiB with no portrait references. Visible and hovered genes hydrate immutable published card details into a 4 MiB revision-keyed cache.
fences.reason: The shoutout risk is sustained daily request and D1 consumption, while the browser risk is cloning cold portrait metadata into every tab and crossing Chromium's 10 MiB storage quota. Separating the compact matcher from bounded on-demand card detail keeps both public infrastructure work and per-user browser cost proportional to real use.
fences.change_control: Anonymous bootstrap, session-presence semantics, catalog, scanner, and card publication metadata, public batch projection, extension scanner migration, storage budgets, cache invalidation, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. The readable marker must never carry identity or authority, transient public-read failures must remain retryable, and portrait references must not return to the per-tab scanner map.

fences.title: Iconoplasm public reads stay cold-safe inside the one loud state boundary
fences.decision: Canonical gene first paint uses a publication-owned O(1) D1 identity index with no portrait or vote fields, then uses the current D1 detail ETag for HTML freshness and checks the HTML cache before detail parsing or rendering. All extracted modules remain behind the existing loudly named single state owner.
fences.reason: Disposable Cloudflare isolates make process warmth an invalid correctness assumption. A broad refactor can also accidentally recreate the retired public-proxy topology if the protective filenames and route owner are treated as ordinary names.
fences.change_control: The cold-path order, published route-membership barrier, current-detail ETag authority, protected filenames, topology manifest, deployment order, module naming rules, tests, instructions, runbook, and production workflow must change atomically. Never put mutable portrait or vote state in the route index; add a second Worker, public proxy, or service-binding hop for normal reads; or replace the protective prefix/suffix with a shortened responsibility-only boundary name.

fences.title: Routine gallery publication is dirty-shard-only
fences.decision: Canonical publish events prepare only their owning content-addressed card shards, in steps of at most six shards per Worker invocation, then atomically flip one manifest. Routine cron and voting paths never rebuild the complete catalog.
fences.reason: The fixed gene universe makes a complete-catalog rebuild unrelated to normal vote scope. The former scattered-delta fallback delayed visible votes, consumed avoidable KV operations, and made an exceptional migration mechanism look like ordinary publication.
fences.change_control: Dirty-symbol event windows, stable shard ownership, local insertion/removal/split behavior, one-step scheduled execution, atomic manifest and watermark order, KV budget accounting, bounded operation audits, migration fail-closed errors, naming rules, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. Never introduce a dirty-count or shard-count threshold that falls back to complete-catalog work.

fences.title: Daily targets give every gene surname one slot
fences.decision: Automatic GeneGuessr daily selection chooses one deterministic representative per normalized gene surname, then selects and falls back only through that one-representative-per-surname sequence. Manual overrides remain explicit exceptions.
fences.reason: Hashing across the flat protein table makes large families proportionally more likely. The surname-balancing schema and practice selector existed, but daily mode bypassed them and automatically selected SLC22A5, SLC6A8, and SLC12A2 in July 2026.
fences.change_control: The source pool, family grouping, deterministic hash, AlphaFold and structure-availability fallback, admin schedule cache version, pre-warm path, request-time path, instructions, runbook, and behavioral tests must change together. Never restore flat-table weighting or adjacent-row fallback.
